_comment: Fixture manifest for the evaluation suite. Each fixture is a deliberately designed test case, not just a sample resume. File paths follow the convention <id>.txt / <id>.expected.json / <id>.extracted.json (simulated extraction for the offline batch demo) / <id>.expected.normalized.json (only when has_normalized_expected is true). 'target' says which pipeline stage the fixture is designed to probe: raw-extraction, normalization, parsing, or graph-construction. 'excluded_near_matches' lists terms that appear in the resume text but must NOT be extracted for that entity type — the tests enforce that they are absent from the gold labels.

fixtures.tests: Baseline: straightforward single-column resume with every entity type present.
failure_modes: missed skills
hallucinated skills
org legal-suffix variation (Acme Analytics, Inc. vs Acme Analytics)
fixtures.notes: The bundled simulated extraction misses Tableau, hallucinates 'Data Science', and returns 'GA4' where the resume says 'Google Analytics 4' — so the demo report shows non-trivial metrics.

fixtures.profile: Career changer (cognitive science research -> consulting -> ML engineering)
fixtures.tests: Preserving career discontinuities across unrelated fields; not hallucinating certifications; not crediting skills that belong to someone else's team.
failure_modes: hallucinated certifications into an empty section
mentioned-but-not-evidenced skill (AWS belongs to the client's team)
fixtures.notes: The resume says Maya 'partnered with the client's AWS infrastructure team' — that is adjacency, not evidence of hands-on AWS use. The bundled simulated extraction falls for this trap on purpose.

fixtures.tests: Non-corporate career structure: appointments, methods-as-skills, publication language; one org node for two roles at the same university.
failure_modes: publication venues or conferences extracted as organizations
duplicate org nodes for repeated affiliations
missed method-style skills
fixtures.notes: Riverbend University hosts two jobs (Adjunct Lecturer, Graduate Research Assistant) but appears once in the organizations gold. Journals and conferences the person published/presented at are not employers.

fixtures.tests: The raw-extraction vs post-normalization boundary: surface abbreviations (ML, NLP, GA4, GCP, CI/CD, RAG, LLM) in the raw gold, canonical labels in the normalized gold; aspirational skills excluded.
failure_modes: extractor silently canonicalizing abbreviations (raw eval should preserve surface forms)
normalizer failing to canonicalize (normalized eval)
aspirational 'interested in learning X' extracted as a skill
fixtures.notes: The only fixture with a second gold file (sample_resume_004.expected.normalized.json). Google Cloud is a certification issuer, not an employer. Two roles at Cascadia Metrics -> one org node.

fixtures.profile: IT systems administrator, messy two-column text
fixtures.tests: Parsing robustness: the .txt simulates naive two-column PDF extraction with interleaved lines, mixed bullet glyphs, and entity names split across lines; org suffix variation plus two roles at the same org.
failure_modes: skills or fields truncated by column splits (VMware vs VMware vSphere, Network vs Network Administration)
duplicate org nodes for 'Northwind Data, LLC' vs 'Northwind Data'
section headers leaking into entities
fixtures.notes: Canonical org name is 'Northwind Data' (suffix stripped). CompTIA is a certification issuer, not an employer. The simulated extraction shows realistic column-split damage.

fixtures.tests: Non-software domain coverage: clinical skills, healthcare orgs, multiple certifications; the soft-skill boundary (PROFILE adjectives are not skills); certification issuers are not organizations.
failure_modes: soft-skill phrases ('compassionate communicator') promoted to skills
certification issuer extracted as an employer
certification abbreviation vs full surface form mismatch (BLS vs Basic Life Support (BLS))

organizations: Board of Certification for Emergency Nursing

fixtures.notes: Certification gold uses the full printed surface form ('Basic Life Support (BLS)'). Raw matching is strict about this — a bare 'BLS' scores as both a miss and an unexpected entity, which is a documented limitation, not a fixture bug.

fixtures.tests: Hallucination resistance: no education or certification sections (both gold lists empty); tool-looking words inside proper names (Python Creek Ventures, Tableau Health Initiative) must not become skills; generic leadership adjectives are not skills.
failure_modes: invented degrees into an empty education list
'Python'/'Tableau' extracted as skills from org/program names
partnership program name extracted as an organization
PROFILE adjectives ('visionary leader', 'strategic thinker') promoted to skills
fixtures.notes: Skills gold is a small set of named, evidenced practices (product strategy, OKRs, A/B testing, roadmap planning). The bundled simulated extraction deliberately fails every trap so the batch report demonstrates detection.
